court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: V.Latha vs The Superintendent Of Police

parties.respondent_defendant: The Superintendent of Police, Thiruvannamalai District; Deputy Inspector General of Police, Vellore Range, Vellore; Inspector General of Police, North Zone, Chennai (Respondents)

facts_of_case: Petitioner challenged the orders passed by respondents imposing penalties. Petitioner was a Head Constable who married Vijayakumar knowing he had an existing wife and children. A charge was framed against her under Rule 3(b) of Tamil Nadu Police Subordinate Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, dated 26.12.2008.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the person who alleges a fact to prove it.
legal_principles.held: The stand of the petitioner that she is not aware of the first marriage of her husband cannot be believed.
cited_cases: V.Latha vs The Superintendent Of Police, (2010)

legal_principles.principle: A panchayat's advice can be a binding decision.
legal_principles.held: On the basis of the advise of Panchayat, they were living separately.
cited_cases: V.Latha vs The Superintendent Of Police, (2010)
